question: v14
q: My power bill in Perth feels huge. Is that just me?

transcript.answer:
**You're not imagining it, but it's mostly not because Perth's power prices jumped.** It's because the government bill credits have run out.

**What the ABS data shows (electricity CPI for Perth, index points):**

| Period | Perth electricity index | What was going on |
|---|---|---|
| Apr–Jun 2024 | 95.18 | Normal tariff, no credits |
| Aug–Sep 2024, Jan–Feb 2025 | **25.71** | Big state and federal credits applied to bills |
| Apr–Jun 2025 | 97.56 | Credits used up |
| Oct 2025–Jan 2026 | 69–90 | Smaller credits only |
| Feb–Jun 2026 | 100.00 | No credits |
| Jul–Aug 2026 | **102.44** | New tariff year, no credits |

**What that means:**
- **The tariff itself has only gone up about 2.5% a year.** You can see it in the months without credits: 95.18, then 97.56, 100, and now 102.44. In August 2026, Perth electricity prices were **up 2.4% on a year earlier**.
- **The ABS counts bill credits as a price cut, so the bill you actually paid swung a lot.** Through much of 2024–25, credits cut the bill you paid by roughly 75% (index 25.71 versus about 97). That's very likely the state's $400 Energy Bill Relief and the federal credit, though the data doesn't name them. Now that they've stopped, the same amount of power costs about four times what you paid in some of those months.
- **Perth is actually doing better than most of the country.** National electricity prices were **up 13.2% in the year to August 2026**, against 2.4% in Perth.

**For context:** Perth's overall inflation was **4.3%** in August 2026, a bit above the national **4.0%**. So your household budget is under pressure in general, and the power bill stands out because the discount has gone.

**If your bill is up a lot more than about 2.5% on a credit-free quarter,** check how much power you used. A hot summer or cold winter, new appliances, or someone home more during the day will push it up. You can also check whether you're on the right tariff with Synergy, such as a time-of-use plan if you have solar or can move your usage to cheaper times.
